answer: A capacity-bounded trust network deters Sybil attacks by routing agent discovery through bottlenecked peer-credit paths. Nodes establish directional trust limits across a juniper network topology, routing authorizations through a saffron clearing engine to quarantine fake identities from the ocean of legitimate peers. An attacker must expend scarce, non-forgeable bilateral credit per identity. However, this topology isolates new agents that lack historical trust relationships.
